aputhujjanasevita.p: [Na+puthujjanasevita] (ti) CL=9 Aputhujjana+sevita] is not practiced- used by the worldlings; practiced-used only by ones who are not worldings- who are noble persons.
a: အပုထုဇ္ဇနသေဝိတ(တိ)
[န+ပုထုဇ္ဇနသေဝိတ။
အပုထုဇ္ဇန+သေဝိတ]  ပုထုဇဉ်တို့သည် မမှီဝဲအပ်သော၊ ပုထုဇဉ်မဟုတ်သူ-အရိယာ-တို့သာမှီဝဲအပ်သော။

B:
aputhujjanasevita：aputhujjanasevita（ti）
အပုထုဇ္ဇနသေဝိတ（တိ）
[na+puthujjanasevita．aputhujjana+sevita]
[န+ပုထုဇ္ဇနသေဝိတ။ အပုထုဇ္ဇန+သေဝိတ]
K:
aputhujjanasevita：အပုထုဇ္ဇနသေဝိတ （တိ）
[န+ပုထုဇ္ဇနသေဝိတ။ အပုထုဇ္ဇန+သေဝိတ]
ပုထုဇဉ်တို့သည် မမှီဝဲအပ်သော၊ ပုထုဇဉ်မဟုတ်သူ-အရိယာ-တို့သာမှီဝဲအပ်သော။
DOP: puthujjana puthujana m.f. [ S. pṛthagjana], 1. an ordinary person (usually not a follower of the Buddha); one who is not a noble one; an outsider; Abh 435 (’nariyo tu ~o); 1084 (nīce ~o mūḷhe); D I 3, 32 (appamattakaṃ kho pan’ etaṃ bhikkhave oramattakaṃ sīlamattakaṃ yena ~o tathāgatassa vaṇṇaṃ vadamāno vadeyya; Sv 59, 15 foll.: so hi puthūnaṃ nānappakārakānaṃ kilesādīnaṃ jananādīhi kāraṇehi ~o … puthu vā ayaṃ visuṃ yeva saṅkhaṃ gato visaṃsaṭṭho sīlasutādiguṇayuttehi ariyehi janehī ti pi ~o ti); M I 8, 29 (diṭṭhisaṃyojanasaṃyutto bhikkhave assutavā ~o na parimuccati jātiyā jarāmaraṇena … upāyāsehi na parimuccati dukkhasmā ti vadāmi); 135, 28 (assutavā ~o ariyānaṃ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto … rūpaṃ etaṃ mama eso ’ham asmi eso me attā ti samanupassati); 323, 24 (idaṃ assa paṭhamaṃ ñāṇaṃ adhigataṃ hoti ariyaṃ lokuttaraṃ asādhāraṇaṃ ~ehi); S II 94, 5 foll. (assutavā bhikkhave ~o imasmiṃ cātumahābhūtikasmiṃ kāyasmiṃ nibbindeyya … yaṃ ca kho etaṃ bhikkhave vuccati cittaṃ iti pi … tatr’ assutavā ~o nālaṃ nibbindituṃ …); 151, 21 (kāmapariyesanaṃ bhikkhave pariyesamāno assutavā ~o tīhi ṭhānehi micchā paṭipajjati kāyena vācāya manasā); III 108, 30 (puriso amaggakusalo ti … ~ass’ etaṃ adhivacanaṃ); A I 10, 14 (assutavato ~assa cittabhāvanā natthī ti); 26, 30 foll. (yaṃ diṭṭhisampanno puggalo kañci saṅkhāraṃ niccato upagaccheyya n’ etaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati … yaṃ ~o kañci saṅkhāraṃ niccato upagaccheyya ṭhānaṃ etaṃ vijjati); III 311, 18* (ete kāmā pavuccanti yattha satto ~o); IV 158, 1 foll. (kiṃ nānākaraṇaṃ sutavato ariyasāvakassa assutavatā ~enā ti); 372, 24 (arahā arahattāya paṭipanno anāgāmī … sotāpanno sotāpattiphalasacchikiriyāya paṭipanno ~o, ime … nava puggalā santo saṃvijjamānā lokasmin ti); Dhp 59 (andhabhūte ~e; Dhp-a I 445, 19 : ~e ti puthūnaṃ kilesānaṃ jananato evaṃ laddhanāme lokiyamahājane); Sn 816 (eko pubbe caritvāna methunaṃ yo nisevati … taṃ loke hīnam āhu ~aṃ); 859 (yena naṃ vajju ~ā atho samaṇabrāhmaṇā); 932 (sutvā rusito bahuṃ vācaṃ samaṇānaṃ vā puthujanānaṃ, Be so; Se puthuvacanānaṃ; Ce, Ee samaṇānaṃ puthuvacanānaṃ; Pj II 565, 5 : tesaṃ samaṇānaṃ vā khattiyādibhedānaṃ vā aññesaṃ puthujanānaṃ, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee puthuvacanānaṃ); Th 215 (apassaṃ ariyasaccāni andhabhūto ~o); Ja V 210, 30 (ye ye ~ā taṃ passanti te te sakabhāvena saṇṭhātuṃ na sakkonti); VI 59, 19* (yattha sanno ~o; 59, 24´ : tattha laggā bahusattā); Nidd I 146, 17 foll. (ken’ atthena ~ā …); Peṭ 180, 13 (kāpurisā vuccanti ~ā); Mil 253, 25 (abhāvitattā mahārāja cittassa ~o kāyikaṃ pi cetasikaṃ pi vedanaṃ vediyati); Sv 59, 7* foll. (duve ~ā vuttā buddhen’ ādiccabandhunā andho ~o eko kalyāṇ’ eko ~o); 998, 36 (tisso sikkhā sikkhatī ti sekho, khīṇāsavo sikkhitasikkhattā puna na sikkhatī ti asekho, ~o sikkhāhi paribāhiyattā nevasekho nāsekho); Ps IV 108, 2 (~o hi yaṃ yaṃ niccaṃ sukhaṃ attā ti gaṇhāti taṃ taṃ ariyasāvako aniccaṃ dukkhaṃ anattā ti gaṇhanto taṃ gāhaṃ vinivaṭṭeti); 109, 22 (mātughātādīni pañca ānantariyakammāni dassitāni honti yāni ~o karoti na ariyasāvako); Mp III 170, 12 (~o hi muṭṭhassati kālaṃ karoti nāma); Saddh 363 (dehaṃ sabhāvato daṭṭhuṃ na sakkonti ~ā); Sadd 626, 27 (putha icc etassa anto saro vyañjane pare ukāro hoti: ~o puthubhūtaṃ); — 2. (being) a follower of the Buddha (a bhikkhu, bhikkhunī or lay person) who has not achieved progress, who has not truly understood the teaching; Vin V 117, 20 (dve puggalā bhabbā sañcicca āpattiṃ āpajjituṃ bhikkhū ca bhikkhuniyo ca ~ā); A I 267, 12 (ekacco puggalo … devānaṃ sahavyataṃ uppajjati … tatra ~o yāvatāyukaṃ ṭhatvā …); Sn 351 (na kāmakāro hi ~ānaṃ saṅkheyyakāro ca tathāgatānaṃ); Vv 82:5 (ahaṃ bhadante ahuvāsi pubbe Sumedhanāmassa jinassa sāvako ~o anavabodho; Vv-a 321, 11 : ~o ti anariyo); Ja II 96, 2 (tesu keci sotāpannā keci sakadāgāmino keci anāgāmino eko pi ~o natthi); 332, 26 (~ā bhikkhū … kujjhiṃsu); Paṭis I 61, 35 (~assa … sekhassa … vītarāgassa …); Pp 13, 5 (satta sekhā bhayūparatā ye ca ~ā sīlavanto arahā abhayūparato); Nett 49, 21 (~assa sotāpannassa ca kāmarāgavyāpādā sādhāraṇā); Mil 162, 5 (upāsako gihī sotāpanno … bhikkhuṃ vā sāmaṇeraṃ vā ~aṃ abhivādeti paccuṭṭheti); Vism 227, 32 (parisuddhasīlādiguṇasamannāgatena ~enā pi [cha anussatiyo] manasikātabbā); Sp 397, 21 foll. (tesu ca bhikkhūsu ~ā pi atthi sotāpannā sakadāgāmī anāgāmī khīṇāsavā); Sv 579, 35 (devatā hi ~e vinivijjha passituṃ sakkonti na khīṇāsave); Ps I 196, 27 foll. (puggalo pana tividho hoti ~o sekho asekho ti, tattha ~o duvidho hoti bāhirako sāsaniko, tattha bāhirako kammavādī kammassakatādiṭṭhiyā sammādiṭṭhi hoti, no saccānulomikāya attadiṭṭhiparāmāsakattā, sāsaniko dvīhi pi); IV 97, 15 (piṇḍapātiko kumbhīlo ti saññāya mahāsaddaṃ akāsi, tadā naṃ ~o ti jāniṃsu); 101, 21 (~o pi pacchimabhaviko ten’ attabhāvena bhavaṃ pariniṭṭhāpetuṃ samattho hoti); 192, 26 (so … pabbajitvā sattāham eva ~o ahosi, aṭṭhame pana so saha paṭisambhidāhi arahattaṃ pāpuṇī ti); Dhp-a I 5, 20 (satthu dhammakathaṃ sutvā pañcakoṭimattā manussā ariyasāvakā jātā dvekoṭimattā ~ā); III 267, 21 (khīṇāsavānaṃ dhammasaṃvego uppajji ~ā assūni dhāretuṃ nāsakkhiṃsu); Pj II 251, 1 (bhikkhū ti sekho vā ~o vā); Nidd-a I 335, 28 (~assa hi saddhā athāvarā padavāre padavāre nānā hoti); Pp-a 247, 25 (~assa nāma gati anibaddhā); Mhv 27:44 (~ā va aṭṭhaṃsu bhikkhū paṭhamabhūmiyaṃ); — ifc see kalyāṇa-; — °- kalyāṇa , m.f. , a person of good habits etc who has not yet attained sotāpatti, but is aiming at such attainment; Nidd-a I 255, 30 foll. (puthujjano ca so kilesānaṃ asamucchinnattā kalyāṇo sīlādipaṭipattiyuttattā ti ~o, ~o eva °-kalyāṇako) = Paṭis-a 507, 1 foll.; — °- kalyāṇaka , m. , °-kalyāṇikā, f. [ BHS pṛthagjanakalyāṇaka], a person of good habits etc who has not yet attained sotāpatti, but is aiming at such attainment; Vin V 2, 31 (ke sikkhanti, sekhā ca ~ā ca sikkhanti); 54, 25 (kā sikkhanti, sekhā ca °-kalyāṇikā); Paṭis I 176, 12 (bhikkhū ti ~o vā hoti bhikkhu sekho vā arahā vā akuppadhammo); II 190, 7 (Paṭis-a 642, 31 : ~assa cā ti nibbānagāminiyā paṭipadāya yuttattā sundaraṭṭhena kalyāṇasaññitassa puthujjanassa); Vism 47, 17 (~ānaṃ sīlaṃ); Ps I 127, 35 (~ena hi saddhiṃ satta sekhā brahmacariyavāsaṃ vasanti nāma); Paṭis-a 205, 11 foll. (andhaputhujjanabhāvaṃ atikamma kalyāṇaputhujjanabhāve ṭhitānaṃ ~ānaṃ kalyāṇaputhujjanānan ti vuttaṃ, puthujjanesu vā kalyāṇakānaṃ ~ānaṃ); Sadd 791, 5 (puthujanassa bhāvo puthujanattanaṃ); — °- tā , f. [ cf BHS pṛthagjanatā], the being an ordinary, unbelieving person; S I 187, 2* (atha saṭṭhisitā savitakkā ~āya adhammaniviṭṭhā, Se so; Be atha saṭṭhinissitā savitakkā puthū janatāya adhammā niviṭṭhā; Ce atha saṭṭhinissitā savitakkā puthujanatāya adhammā niviṭṭhā; Ee atha saṭṭhitasitā vitakkā puthujanatāya adhammā niviṭṭhā; Ee atha saṭṭhisitā savitakkā puthū janatāya adhammaniviṭṭhā) = Th 1217 ( Se so; Be adhammā; Ce, Ee aṭṭhasaṭṭhisitā; Ee puthujjanatāya; cf Th-a III 190, 35 : te pana micchāvitakkā niccādigāhavasena adhammā dhammato apetā ~āya andhabāle niviṭṭhā); — °- dussīla , m.f. , an ordinary person of poor moral habits; M III 255, 11 (Ps V 71, 13 : ~ā nāma kevaṭṭamacchabandhādayo parapīḷāya jīvikaṃ kappetā); — °- sīlava(t) , m.f. , an ordinary person of good moral habits; M III 255, 9 (Ps V 71, 10 : °-sīlavā nāma gosīladhātuko hoti, asaṭho amāyāvī paraṃ apīḷetvā dhammena samena kasiyā vā vaṇijjāya vā jīvikaṃ kappetā); Sv 584, 4 ; — aputhujjanasevita , m.f. , (what is) cultivated by those who are not ordinary people, by noble ones; (what is) not cultivated by ordinary people; S I 133, 20* (akampitaṃ acalitaṃ ~aṃ) ≠ Thī 201 (Thī-a 165, 29 : buddhādīhi ariyehi eva gocarabhāvanābhigamato sevitattā ~am); Dhp 272 (phusāmi nekkhammasukhaṃ ~aṃ; Dhp-a III 400, 2 : puthujjanehi asevitaṃ ariyasevitam eva); — see also pothujjanika.
CPD: a-puthujjana-sevita , mfn., unheeded by the vulgar; acc. ~am (a-kampitaṃ a-tuliyaṃ +, scil. dhammaṃ), Thī 201.

aputta.p: [Na+putta] (pu) Google Translate (1) He is not a son. He was abandoned as a son. (2) A son who is insulted and disgusted.
a: (၁)သားမဟုတ်သူ။ သားအဖြစ်မှ စွန့်အပ်သူ၊ သားမတော်စပ်သူ။(၂)ကဲ့ရဲ့-စက်ဆုပ်-အပ်သော သား။

B:
aputta：aputta（pu）
အပုတ္တ（ပု）
[na+putta]
[န+ပုတ္တ]
K:
aputta：အပုတ္တ（ပု）
[န+ပုတ္တ]
（၁） သားမဟုတ်သူ။ သားအဖြစ်မှ စွန့်အပ်သူ၊ သားမတော်စပ်သူ။ （၂） ကဲ့ရဲ့-စက်ဆုပ်-အပ်သော သား။
DOP: putta putra m. ( pl. nom./acc. ~e ~āni) [ S. putra], 1. a son (of men or birds or animals); pl. also sons and daughters, children; Abh 240; 249 (~ā tu puttadhītaro); Vin I 83, 13 (na bhikkhave ananuññāto mātāpitūhi ~o pabbājetabbo); 147, 22 (ahaṃ hi gilānā āgacchatu me ~o icchāmi ~assa āgatan ti); III 26, 7 (~o me atthi so mayā posetabbo ti); 66, 35 (~o kho āvuso pituno dāyajjo ti); D I 135, 27 (manussā ca mudā modamānā ure ~e naccentā apārutagharā maññe viharissantī ti); II 272, 7 (Sakkassa devānam indassa °-ttaṃ ajjhūpagatā); III 189, 5 (pañcahi … ṭhānehi ~ena puratthimā disā mātāpitaro paccupaṭṭhātabbā); M I 333, 8 (tassa me Kāḷī nāma bhaginī tassā tvaṃ ~o so me tvaṃ bhāgineyyo hosi); S I 42, 16* (~o pavadataṃ varo; Spk I 98, 20 : rājakulamajjhādīsu pavadantānaṃ ~o varo, so hi mātāpitūnaṃ anatthāvahaṃ na vadati); 210, 12* (piyo loke sako ~o); A III 43, 22* (pañcaṭṭhānāni sampassaṃ ~am icchanti paṇḍitā); 44, 3* (ovādakārī bhataposī kulavaṃsaṃ ahāpayaṃ saddho sīlena sampanno ~o hoti pasaṃsiyo); 148, 24 (pañcahi bhikkhave aṅgehi samannāgato rañño cakkavattissa jeṭṭho ~o pitarā pavattitaṃ cakkaṃ dhammen’ eva anupavatteti); Dhp 288 (na santi ~ā tāṇāya); Ud 5, 29 (eso te samaṇa ~o posa nan ti); 17, 33 (iccheyyāmāhaṃ bhagavā aññāni pi evarūpāni satta ~ānī ti; Ud-a 157, 11 foll.: aññe pi evarūpe satta ~e ti vattabbe liṅgavipallāsena vuttaṃ); It 62, 20 (tayo ’me bhikkhave ~ā … atijāto anujāto avajāto ti); Sn 35 (na ~am iccheyya kuto sahāyaṃ eko care khaggavisāṇakappo); 38 (~esu dāresu ca yā apekhā; Pj II 76, 5 : puttadhītubhariyāsu); 149 (mātā yathā niyaṃ ~aṃ āyusā ekaputtam anurakkhe); 255 (yasmiṃ ca seti urasīva ~o sa ve mitto); 858 (na tassa ~ā pasavo khettaṃ vatthuṃ ca vijjati, so read with Be, Ce, Se ); Vv 83:11 (ko vā tvaṃ kassa vā ~o kathaṃ jānemu taṃ mayaṃ); Pv 6:3 (pañca ~āni … vijāyitvāna); 42:5 (thaṇḍile pattaṃ bhinditvā hasamāno apakkami rañño Kitavass’ ahaṃ ~o, kiṃ maṃ bhikkhu karissasi); Th 475 (kicchā laddho ayaṃ ~o … imaṃ dadāma te nātha); Thī 312 (petāni bhoti ~āni khādamānā tuvaṃ pure); Ja II 19, 4 (tassa pana hatthissa ~o sabbaseto hatthājānīyapotako atthi); 39, 12 (apare pan’ assa dve haṃsapotakā ~ā ahesuṃ); III 50, 13* (tātā ti ~o vadamāno kampeti hadayaṃ pitu); V 279, 13 (avassaṃ ettikāsu itthīsu ekā puññavatī ~aṃ labhissatī ti); 509, 22* (na te ~ā ye na bharanti jiṇṇaṃ); VI 133, 2* (~ehi deva yajitabbaṃ; 133, 6´ : attano jātehi piyaputtehi c’ eva piyadhītāhi ca); 290, 14* (āmantaya vammadharāni … ~āni; 290, 20´ : mama ~e ca dhītaro ca); 380, 21* (puttass’ āvikareyya guyham atthaṃ); 528, 23* (yattha Vessantaro rājā saha ~ehi sammati); Nidd I 247, 31 foll. (cattāro ~ā attajo ~o khettajo ~o dinnako ~o antevāsiko ~o); Ap 330, 29 (bhariyā me kālakatā ~o sīvathikaṃ gato); 355, 13 (kiṃ me ~ehi dārehi rajjena sakalena ca); Cp 3:2:1 (kāmito dayito ~o); Mil 75, 14 foll. (api ca mātusadiso vā ~o hoti mātupakkho vā pitusadiso vā ~o hoti pitupakkho vā ti); 287, 29 (~ā mahārāja loke bandhanaṃ); Vism 567, 27 (pitito nāmavasena ~o); Mp I 258, 8 (Rāhulasāmaṇero pitu anucchaviko ~o ti); 399, 7 (rūpūpajīviniyo ca nāma vijātakāle sace ~o hoti chaḍḍenti sace dhītā jagganti); Dhp-a I 88, 25 (Upatissagāmake jeṭṭhakulassa °-ttā Upatisso ti nāmaṃ kariṃsu); II 273, 17 (yassa gehe ~o vā dhītā vā na koci matapubbo ti); Ud-a 276, 14 (vijātamātuyā nāma virūpo pi ~o surūpo viya manāpo hoti, Be, Se so; Ce, Ee piyamanāpo hoti); Pj II 79, 3 (deva kulavaṃsānupālako ~o icchitabbo attaje avijjamāne khettajo pi kulavaṃsadharo hotī ti); Th-a III 127, 13 (rañño ekā dhītā va atthi ~o natthi, arājakaṃ rajjaṃ nassati, Be, Ce, Se so; Ee arājikaṃ rajjaṃ na nandati); Nidd-a I 258, 3 (puṃ tāyati rakkhatī ti ~o); Sadd 402, 11 foll. aputtaka.p: [Na+putta+ka] (ti) CL=8 look page 341 in padarūpasiddhi, in the feminine gender aputtikā, having no son, having no inheritor, who does not have a son
pn:
Aputtaka. A wealthy burgess of Sāvatthī who died intestate. In the Saṁyuttanikāya (SN.i.89-91) we find Pasenadi, King of Kosala, visiting the Buddha at noonday and telling him that he had just finished having the banker’s wealth removed to the royal coffers, “eight millions of gold to say nothing of silver.” And yet Aputtaka ate nothing except sour husk-gruel left over from the previous day and wore only hempen garments.

In the next Sutta of the same Nikāya (SN.i.91-3) the Buddha is reported as revealing the banker’s past. In a former birth he had given alms to a Pacceka Buddha, Tagarasikhī, but later he regretted it and wished that he had given the food to slaves and workmen.

He had, in the same birth, slain the only son of his brother for the sake of his fortune.

As a result of the alms he was born seven times in the Deva-worlds and seven times as a rich man of Sāvatthī. His regret made him inclined to deny himself enjoyment of sense-desires. Owing to the murder of his nephew in his previous birth, he was childless in this, and he died intestate. After this life he was born in Mahā Roruva purgatory.

The Mayhakajātaka (Ja.iii.299f.), contains the whole story of the banker’s past and present, giving many graphic details not found in the Saṁyutta account, but it does not mention the seven births in heaven or in Sāvatthī. It adds that the king’s men took seven days and nights to remove the treasure. Aputtaka is there referred to not as Aputtaka but as Āgantuka (Stranger). See also Dhp-a.iv.76-80.
